newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Taleban launch attack on Kunduz in north.
newsitem.headline: Taleban launch attack on Kunduz in north.

text.p: Afghanistan's purist Islamic Taleban militia said on Tuesday its forces based in the northern town of Baghlan had launched an overnight offensive towards the city of Kunduz, about 65 km (40 miles) further north.

Taleban officials, quoted by the Pakistan-based Afghan Islamic Press (AIP), said their fighters had captured the town of Aliabad 40 km (25 miles), north of Baghlan, on Tuesday morning and had gone on to seize Kunduz airport.
The officials said fighting was now going on near the city of Kunduz, which is held by various opposition factions. There was no independent account of the reported offensive.
"Some local commanders invited us to come to Kunduz," a Kandahar-based Taleban official, Wakil Ahmad, told AIP.
The Taleban force, estimated at about 3,000 strong, arrived in Baghlan last week after opposition forces drove it from the town of Pul-i-Khumri, 30 km (19 miles) south of Baghlan.
